findings.description: Direct inspection of all five V193 views and six pose renders: the neutral skirt still has dense irregular vertical folds and a ragged waist junction. Crouch and sit retain broad exposed anterior thighs; pose coverage is still insufficient.

V193 front, side, three-quarter, back, and prone views still show angular planar folds across the bodice, a gray waist patch with unverified garment-surface ownership, and an uneven waist/back transition. Bodice appearance remains unacceptable.

The new authored-pattern row reconstruction anchors 108 lap-hem vertices and 262 shared panel-boundary vertices, but orientation-safe scales remain low (front-lap-left 0.0137, front-lap-right 0.0171, front-left 0.1135, front-right 0.1329); effective mean blend is 0.0356 and maximum rest displacement is 0.0032 m. Anterior-thigh ray hits are 48/532 in crouch and 22/532 in sit. This is only a small diagnostic change and is not fit acceptance.

nextAction: Stop iterating on point-placement scale and row width: the V193 row-wise reconstruction remains constrained by face inversion and did not materially improve crouch/sit coverage or the visible skirt folds. Inspect the current evaluated cloth topology and pose-matched mesh in Blender to identify why the authored front-lap panels cannot reach the evaluated thighs while preserving seams and hem; change the actual panel geometry/cloth construction or pose deformation model before another trial. Keep the exact authored hems/shared seams, reject the faceted bodice and gray waist patch until separately corrected, and continue to block fit, Shape Key, Unity/VRChat, package, and release.
